$comment: ONTOLOGY SCHEMA for the BMS minimized V-model. Wired via
`[needs] schema_definitions_from_json = "schemas.json"` in ubproject.toml and
checked by `ubc schema validate` and by the sphinx-needs build.
JSON carries no comments, so the rationale lives here and in each rule's
`message`. Every rule below was derived from two sources and nothing else:
DECLARED  -- `[[workflow.stages.trace]]` (link / direction / min / up) and
`[[needs.types]] prefix` in ubproject.toml. These are the
obligations the project already states, so they are `violation`.
OBSERVED  -- a census of the 194-need graph taken when this file was written.
Where the data is unanimous but no config declares the rule, it is
recorded at `warning` so it guides authors without hard-failing a
build on a convention the project never committed to.
THIS FILE DOES NOT CHECK BACKWARD COVERAGE, and that is deliberate. Read this
before adding a `network_back` rule -- one was added here once and removed.
An OUTGOING obligation is owed by the need being authored, at the moment it is
authored: a req written without `traces_to` is wrong on the spot and its author
can fix it alone. Those are the `trace-*` rules below, and they are violations.
An INCOMING obligation is owed by a LATER STAGE. `arch <- refines` is owed by
`swreqs`, which `depends_on = ["archs"]`, so it is unmet BY CONSTRUCTION for as
long as that stage is pending. That is a V-model project in motion, not a defect,
and it is ALREADY GATED: the five `direction = "both"` trace edges in
ubproject.toml are exactly the five backward legs, and `ubc agent gaps` reports
each unmet one as a tracked `gap` need, puts it on traceability.rst, and points
`ubc agent next` at the stage that owes the work. CI runs that gate separately
and deliberately does not fail on it.
Five `coverage-*-back` rules used to live here and were a strict duplicate of
those five edges. They cost more than they were worth. As violations they failed
the build on three arch needs that were exactly where the workflow expected them
to be. Demoted to warnings they still failed `ubc check`, WHICH EXITS 1 ON A
WARNING -- so they turned the project's one deliberate demo gap into red CI. And
silencing them needed `[lint] ignore`, which blanks them out of
`ubc schema validate` too, leaving rules that fired nowhere. Deleting them fixed
the cause instead of the symptom, and took the conf.py `suppress_warnings` entry
with it.
So: coverage is the gap gate's; SHAPE is this file's. If you want a coverage
obligation, add a `direction = "both"` trace edge in ubproject.toml -- do not
add it here.
The census, AS A SNAPSHOT and nothing more (194 needs / 194 links):
user_story 4   req 19   arch 14   swreq 23   impl 23
test 50        test_result 50    risk 5    decision 5   gap 1
Every outgoing trace link resolved to exactly one target type, and every
non-root need carried at least one -- those are the facts the `violation` rules
rest on, and they are properties of the ONTOLOGY, true of any state the graph
can be in. Do not set a severity from a count that only holds in a finished
graph; that is the mistake the deleted rules were built on.
THIS FILE vs ubproject.toml. A field is GLOBAL in ubCode: declared once,
present on every type, left at its `default` on the types that do not use it.
So a `schema` on `[needs.fields.<name>]` states what is true of the field
EVERYWHERE -- which for the imported fields means "" must be admissible, since
that is what the ~190 needs outside the owning type carry. Narrowing a field on
the one type that owns it is THIS file's job, keyed by `select`.
A VOCABULARY IS WRITTEN EXACTLY ONCE, and the trick that keeps it that way is
worth knowing before adding a rule. A global enum has to admit "", so it reads
`"" | <the valid values>`; excluding "" on the owning type therefore yields the
valid values with no second copy of the list. So the per-type rule says
`minLength: 1`, NOT the enum again:
outcome         field: "" | passed | failed | error | skipped
here:  minLength 1  ->  exactly those four on test_result
test_run_label  field: "" | the non-ISO timestamp form
here:  minLength 1  ->  a real timestamp on test_result
status          field: draft | review | approved
here:  WHICH TYPES OWE ONE -- the six authored types
gap_category    field: nothing (see field-gap-category for why)
here:  the seven categories, at `warning`
If you find yourself pasting an enum from ubproject.toml into this file, stop:
the answer is almost always `minLength: 1`. Put a constraint here only when it
is type-specific; if it holds for every need, it belongs on the field.
WHICH CONSTRUCT DOES WHAT -- each check is written once, in the one place that
can express it, with no overlap between them:
local.properties.<link>.minItems + local.required   HOW MANY outgoing links.
A link field is a plain array of target ids, so arity is an ordinary array
constraint -- NOT network `contains` + `minContains`, which is a weaker way
of saying the same thing (it bounds only the MATCHING items) and duplicates
the type test `items` already does.
`required` IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE. `properties` constrains a key only when it
is present, and a need carrying no link at all has no such key -- so
`minItems` ALONE SILENTLY PASSES on exactly the case these rules exist to
catch. Probed: `minItems: 1` on the 4 user_story needs (which have no
`traces_to`) fired 0 times; adding `required` fired 4. Never write one
without the other. `maxItems` needs no `required` -- an absent field
trivially satisfies an upper bound, which is the intended reading.
network.<link>.items                                WHAT TYPE the targets are.
Applies to every element, which is the intent: a req traces only to user
stories. Probed on its own (no `contains`) against a deliberately wrong
type: fired on all 23 swreqs.
COSMETIC NOTE: when a rule carries both `local` and `network` and the LOCAL
half fails, the finding is reported TWICE with the same message -- once as
local_other, once as network_local_fail -- because the network walk
re-applies the rule's local schema as a precondition. Two identical lines
are one defect, not two. A network-only failure reports once.
network_back.<link>.contains + minContains          INCOMING coverage.
The ONLY construct available here. Incoming links are not locally visible:
a `local` rule on a declared incoming field name (`satisfied_by`,
`verifies_back`, ...) matches nothing and silently passes. Probed and
confirmed -- never reach for `local` on an incoming link.
TWO KEYWORDS THAT LOOK PORTABLE AND ARE NOT. ubCode accepts both; sphinx-needs
rejects both, and the file is consumed by BOTH engines:
- `not` inside a `select` allOf element -- `ubc check` flags this one as
config.schema_sphinx_needs_incompatible.
- `not` inside a `local` field constraint -- `ubc check` does NOT flag it;
only sphinx-build does, as a hard NeedsConfigException. Prefer a positive
`pattern` (see field-test_result-run-label-not-iso).
So `ubc check` passing is not sufficient: run the ubtrace build too.
A SYNTAX ERROR ANYWHERE DISABLES THE WHOLE FILE (ubc reports it against the
pseudo-need `__config__` and applies no rule at all), so re-run both validators
after every edit rather than trusting a clean build.

schemas.message: DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives user_story the prefix US_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives req the prefix REQ_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives arch the prefix ARCH_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives swreq the prefix SWREQ_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives impl the prefix IMPL_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives test the prefix TEST_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives test_result the prefix TRES_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives risk the prefix RISK_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives decision the prefix DEC_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives gap the prefix GAP_.
DECLARED (stage `reqs`, trace link=traces_to min=1 up=user_story): every req must trace up to a user_story. OBSERVED 19/19.

DECLARED (stage `archs`, trace link=satisfies min=1 up=req): every arch must satisfy at least one req. OBSERVED 14/14, fan-out 1..4 -- the upper end is left unbounded, an observed maximum is not a rule.
DECLARED (stage `swreqs`, trace link=refines min=1 up=arch): every swreq must refine an arch. OBSERVED 23/23.
DECLARED (stage `code`, trace link=implements min=1 up=swreq): every impl marker must implement a swreq. OBSERVED 23/23.
DECLARED (stage `tests`, trace link=verifies min=1 up=swreq): every test marker must verify a swreq. OBSERVED 50/50.

DECLARED (stage `test_results`, trace link=results_for min=1 up=test) plus a STRUCTURAL upper bound: one recorded outcome belongs to exactly one test case in exactly one run, so a second target would make the evidence unattributable. Both bounds are violations, so they share one rule. OBSERVED 50/50, all exactly 1.
DECLARED (stage `risks`, trace link=mitigates min=1 up=req): every risk must bear on at least one req. OBSERVED 5/5, fan-out 1..2, upper end left unbounded.
DECLARED (stage `decisions`, trace link=affects min=1 up=arch): every decision must constrain at least one arch. OBSERVED 5/5, fan-out 1..2, upper end left unbounded.

OBSERVED 1/1: an imported gap must attribute itself to exactly one need. No `items` type test, because a gap can legitimately be raised against any type. `gap_for` is deliberately named by no stage trace edge -- an obligation to carry a gap would make a clean graph fail the gap gate -- so this rule only checks the shape the importer writes.

OBSERVED 19/19: a req traces to exactly one user_story. Convention, not declared config -- a req that genuinely serves two stories is a design smell worth a second look, not an error. Kept separate from trace-req-traces_to because that rule's lower bound is declared and this upper bound is not.
OBSERVED 23/23, and stated in ubproject.toml: a swreq refines THE arch element whose behaviour it pins down -- singular. Two parents means the behaviour belongs to neither component cleanly.
OBSERVED 23/23: one impl marker realises one swreq. The one-line marker grammar accepts a list, so this is a convention the grammar does not enforce.
OBSERVED 50/50: one test marker covers one swreq. A test asserting against two requirements at once is hard to attribute when it fails.

OBSERVED 50/50 non-empty: tools/import_test_results.py stamps outcome, runtime_s, test_run_label and chain_reqs on every generated result. Fields are global in ubCode and default to "", so this checks they were actually POPULATED, not merely present -- an empty one means the importer half-wrote the need. NOTE THAT NON-EMPTY IS ALL THIS RULE HAS TO SAY, even for the two fields that have a vocabulary: `[needs.fields]` already admits exactly `"" | <the valid values>` for both, so excluding "" here yields the valid values without this file restating them. outcome becomes exactly `passed | failed | error | skipped`, and test_run_label exactly the non-ISO timestamp form. Writing the enum out again would be a second copy to keep in sync, and the vocabulary belongs on the field because it holds for every need, not just this type.

WARNING, NOT VIOLATION, ON PURPOSE. These are the seven categories the 0.34 engine emits, per CATEGORIES in tools/import_gaps.py -- but that importer renders an UNKNOWN category generically rather than rejecting it, because `ubc agent` is alpha and "a gate finding must never be dropped because this table has not caught up with the engine". A violation here would invert that: a newer engine emitting an eighth category would fail the build instead of reporting the gap. At `warning` the drift is surfaced -- go add the new category to CATEGORIES and to this list -- while the finding still lands. This is also why `[needs.fields.gap_category]` in ubproject.toml carries no global enum.

OBSERVED 1/1 non-empty: tools/import_gaps.py stamps gap_category, gap_need_id and gap_need_type on every generated gap. gap_need_id duplicates the gap_for link on purpose -- a report template cannot walk links, so the field is the half a Jinja report can read.

PRESENCE only -- the VALUE is constrained globally by `[needs.fields.status]` in ubproject.toml (enum draft/review/approved), which is the right home for it because the vocabulary is the same wherever a status appears. This rule adds the half a global schema cannot express: WHICH TYPES OWE ONE. All 70 authored spec needs (user_story, req, arch, swreq, risk, decision) carry a status; the four derived types (impl, test, test_result, gap) carry none, correctly -- their state is the source file or the import, not a lifecycle -- and `status` is nullable precisely so they can. Raised from warning to violation now that the vocabulary is declared: a spec need with no status is no longer an unwritten convention.
